one_liner: Run and improve the National Gallery of Art's warehouse asset and inventory system: tracking property, moving furniture and equipment, and handling disposal of excess items.
fit_summary: Daniel may qualify on education: the posting accepts a master's degree in place of the specialized experience, and he has an M.A. from George Mason (2016), though HR decides whether Global Affairs counts. The work (tracking property and equipment, moving furniture, disposing of excess items) is close to his IEM logistics: procuring and tracking medical supplies for sites in six states and building order-status reports. The catch is the GS-9 ceiling and a narrow, warehouse-focused job.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status, clearance or veterans' preference needed.
One year of specialized experience at the GS-07 equivalent, serving as a focal point for implementing an asset management system for a warehouse operation, must be met by 11/02/2026.
Alternative: a master's degree, 2 full years of graduate education, a related LL.B./J.D., or a qualifying combination of education and experience.
Must pass a background investigation, be registered with Selective Service if male and born after 12/31/59, and may serve a probationary period.
keywords: reutilization and disposal of excess equipment
strategy: Lead with the six-state supply tracking (2021 to 2022), the vendor relationships, and the office deliveries and conference supplies he handled, in the posting's terms: inventory, property accountability, receiving and disposal.
List the M.A. (George Mason, May 2016) and upload the transcript, since the posting accepts a master's in place of the specialized experience.
Preview the questionnaire and answer only at levels your resume supports; overstating can remove you from consideration.
Keep the resume to two pages, with month/year dates, hours per week, and a short bullet set that uses the posting's exact logistics terms.
Apply well before the 11/02/2026 close; the window is only two weeks.
For a better fit, target 0343 analyst, emergency management (0089), or legislative and public affairs roles at FEMA, Virginia VDEM, Prince William County, or congressional offices.
resume_bullets: As part of the logistics team, procured and tracked medical supplies, equipment and vaccines across six states for COVID-19 mass care sites, with Excel pivot-table reports on order status and spending (2021–2022).
Set up relationships with medical supply, truck rental and other vendors to keep sites stocked.
Handled deliveries and conference supplies as part of office manager duties at IEM (2019–2024).
interview_questions: Describe a time you implemented or improved an inventory or asset tracking system. What was your role?
How would you decide which warehouse processes to change or automate?
Walk us through how you would handle disposal or reutilization of excess federal property.
How do you keep property records accurate when many customers are requesting moves and supplies?
watch_outs: The specialized experience is very specific (warehouse asset management), so the M.A. is his likeliest way to qualify.
Promotion potential is capped at GS-09, and the role doesn't use Daniel's policy and public-facing strengths.
Commuting from Manassas to downtown DC; telework is available, but the role is not remote and warehouse work likely requires on-site time.
